title: Five inbox loaders still discard the skipped-file warnings, so a broken file there is absent with no trace
summary: PR #1042 made triage's inbox section, the CLI, wave supply and the dashboard name an unreadable inbox file. Five other call sites still call inboxbatch.LoadDir and drop the warnings: triagecap/wave_seed.go:27 (candidate seeding), core/lane_scope_assembly.go:39, core/retry_tier_escalation.go:72, phases/triage/unified.go:47 and :51. A numeric priority no longer reaches them (the decoder reads it), so only a genuinely unreadable file is lost there, but wave seeding still treats it as absent with no record.
fix: Move each site to inboxbatch.ScanDir and surface DirScan.Warnings with LoadWarning.String through that site's own channel (a stderr WARN line or a signal), or fail closed with DirScan.HasUnreadable where the site must not act on a partial inbox. core/ is a protected surface: keep the change minimal and pinned by tests.
acceptance: Each of the five sites names an unreadable inbox file on an operator-visible channel, or refuses on DirScan.HasUnreadable, pinned by a test with one malformed file
No production call site discards the warnings of inboxbatch.LoadDir (a grep-level guard test)

consumed.resolution: the five sites read inboxbatch.ScanDir: wave seed, LaneDeclaredFiles (refuses on HasUnreadable), processingClaimIDs and the two unified-commitment loads name each skipped file; TestNoProductionCodeCallsLoadDir refuses any production call of LoadDir
